Olga / Kim — technical notes below to include in the consolidated packet.

- Backups and purge cadence: Redwood takes daily snapshots of customer volumes and retains them for 90 days as the standard backup window for quick restores; long-term archival snapshots are kept up to 18 months depending on the account plan. Permanent deletion from backups (tombstone + overwrite) is scheduled in phased waves — metadata tombstones at T+90, block-level zeroization between T+120 and T+180 depending on replication and compaction schedules. We can provide the purge job run logs (example attached).

- Temporary holds: we support per-tenant temporary retention holds via the retention orchestration API. Holds are recorded with a request id, issuer, scope (data classes), and TTL. Standard hold TTL is 180 days; extensions require legal sign-off and are logged in the audit trail.

- Logs: security/forensic logs are in a separate retention class. Default is 365 days for security logs; application-level request logs are 90 days. Exception approvals live in the approvals ledger (audit id references).

- Subprocessors & transfers: current subprocessor registry includes (high level): S3-compatible object store (us-east-1), analytics provider (EU-hosted), DataEscrow Inc. (custody/escrow). Cross-border transfers occur for analytics and escalation support — covered under DPA Clause 6.3 (standard SCCs applied where relevant).

Next steps: I'll extract purge-run exemplar logs for Medix (filtered to your tenant IDs) and drop into a secure Share link. Also prepared a short JSON manifest showing hold request records.
